$comment_cardImageQuality: standard). These are luxury-market listing photos where compression
artefacts in brickwork, window mullions and fabric are visible and
unacceptable. 85 is already in the qualities allow-list because
BILLING, stated precisely. Quality does NOT add candidate widths, so
it does not multiply the ladder. But quality IS part of the
optimizer cache key, so raising it:
- abandons the entire existing q=75 card cache, and
- costs ONE new transformation + ONE cache write per
source-width pair, the first time each is requested at q=85.
Repeat requests are then cache reads. So this is a one-time
re-population, not a recurring charge — but it is NOT 'bytes only',
and the scenario costs recorded in
ARE that re-population cost, incurred as traffic touches each pair.

$comment_minimumCacheTTL: SAFE BECAUSE THE CACHE KEY IS THE SOURCE URL, AND BOTH MEDIA HOSTS
MINT A NEW URL WHEN THE UNDERLYING PHOTO CHANGES:
R2       — object keys embed an epoch-ms mint stamp, e.g.
/listings/SL-0004/1780109874725-hero.webp
Cotality — the MediaURL path embeds a Unix timestamp; the segment
'MjAvMjE1MjYvMTc4NTQ5MDYzMA' base64-decodes to
per-object signature segment
So a replaced or re-synced photo produces a DIFFERENT optimizer
cache key, and a short TTL would only re-transform identical bytes
under a new cache-write charge.
SCOPE OF THAT GUARANTEE — stated precisely, because the earlier
wording was too absolute. This TTL cannot mask a changed source URL
ONCE THE DTO HANDS THE NEW URL TO THE OPTIMIZER. It says nothing
about whether the stored URL was refreshed in the first place.
The known #586 defect can leave media_url_original unrefreshed on
active, unmirrored, parked rows; in that case the DTO keeps handing
the optimizer an obsolete URL and the image is stale at source, not
in this cache. Media freshness is a SEPARATE contract, fixed by the
media_url_original freshness hotfix — not by anything in this file.

$comment_gallery: LISTING-DETAIL GALLERY (2026-11-02). Measured on an emulated 820px tablet,
Slow 4G, a 17-photo listing: 6.9 MB transferred (5.9 MB images), LCP 27.8s.
R2 stores ONE full-resolution file per synced photo and the DTO's thumbUrl
equals url, so the strip's 88px thumbnails each downloaded the original.
Every width below is already in deviceSizes / imageSizes, every quality is
already in qualities, and no host is added: this changes WHO asks the
optimizer, not what the optimizer admits.
galleryImageWidths — the main viewer, full-bleed on phones, 1600px max above.
1440px @2x needs 2880 -> 3840. The optimizer never upscales past the
source, so the top rung returns at most the original: never worse than the
raw URL it replaces. (Premium standard, 2026-08-01: never under-resolve.)
galleryThumbWidths — 88 CSS px thumbnails: 3x needs 264 -> 384 rung.
galleryFullscreenWidths — the lightbox (<=95vw, <=92vh), asked at 100vw so
it never under-resolves; quality 90, as the heroes use.
$comment_galleryOptimizerHosts: COMPLIANCE POLICY (2026-11-02 pre-merge review). The gallery may hand ONLY Mallan's own R2 host to the
optimizer. Cotality photos (api.cotality.com, normally reached through /api/media/proxy) stay on the existing
proxy: it adds the bearer authorization, validates the response and caches 7 days, whereas the optimizer
would fetch the provider URL directly and keep a transformed copy for minimumCacheTTL (31 days). Whether the
IDX Plus agreement permits that for the detail gallery, and what must happen to those copies when a
listing is withdrawn or its media authorization changes, is NOT established. Until it is certified this list
must not contain a Cotality host. It is a strict subset of optimizerTrustedHosts (a test enforces both).
The search cards' existing behaviour (which does optimize Cotality photos) is not changed by this key.
THIS IS A HOST-LEVEL CONTROL, NOT A CONTENT-LEVEL ONE. Mallan's R2 can hold copies of Cotality-feed photos
(the media sync mirrors the hero photo of every displayable third-party listing, and galleries mirrored
earlier stay in the bucket), and those R2 URLs DO reach the optimizer. What this key guarantees is only that
no api.cotality.com URL does. Also open: there is no purge path for a transformed copy once issued (Vercel
supports invalidation by source image; nothing here calls it), and the copy may outlive the 31-day
minimumCacheTTL because R2 objects are served with max-age=31536000 (how the optimizer combines the two is
not verified). Rights to store, transform and CDN-cache are not established in this repo.
